name.text: Surface area of a frustum made from a cone.

questiontext.text:
A right circular cone is cut by a plane parallel to its base, producing a frustum. The frustum has:

  • lower radius \(R={@R@}\),
  • upper radius \(r={@r@}\),
  • vertical height \(h={@h@}\).
[[jsxgraph]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid,{ boundingbox:[-15,16,15,-3], axis:false, showNavigation:false, showCopyright:false, keepaspectratio:true }); var R={#R#}; var r={#r#}; var h={#h#}; var ey=0.28; /* ---------- Bottom ellipse ---------- */ var xb=[],yb=[]; for(var t=0;t<=360;t+=3){ xb.push(R*Math.cos(t*Math.PI/180)); yb.push(ey*R*Math.sin(t*Math.PI/180)); } board.create('curve',[xb,yb],{ strokeWidth:2, fillColor:'#4F79C7', fillOpacity:0.85 }); /* ---------- Top ellipse ---------- */ var xt=[],yt=[]; for(var t=0;t<=360;t+=3){ xt.push(r*Math.cos(t*Math.PI/180)); yt.push(h+ey*r*Math.sin(t*Math.PI/180)); } board.create('curve',[xt,yt],{ strokeWidth:2, fillColor:'#4F79C7', fillOpacity:0.85 }); /* ---------- Side edges ---------- */ board.create('segment',[[-R,0],[-r,h]],{ strokeWidth:2 }); board.create('segment',[[R,0],[r,h]],{ strokeWidth:2 }); /* ---------- Height ---------- */ board.create('arrow',[[0,h],[0,0]],{strokeWidth:2}); board.create('arrow',[[0,0],[0,h]],{strokeWidth:2}); board.create('text',[ 0.6, h/2, '\\(' + h + '\\,\\mathrm{cm}\\)' ]); /* ---------- Top radius ---------- */ board.create('arrow',[ [0,h], [-0.72*r,h-0.72*ey*r] ],{ strokeWidth:2 }); board.create('text',[ -r/2-0.8, h+0.4, '\\(' + r + '\\,\\mathrm{cm}\\)' ]); /* ---------- Bottom radius ---------- */ board.create('arrow',[ [0,0], [-0.72*R,-0.72*ey*R] ],{ strokeWidth:2 }); board.create('text',[ -R/2-1, -1, '\\(' + R + '\\,\\mathrm{cm}\\)' ]); /* ---------- Slant height ---------- */ board.create('arrow',[ [R,0], [r,h] ],{ strokeWidth:2 }); board.create('text',[ R+0.7, h/2, '\\({@sdisp@}\\,\\mathrm{cm}\\)' ]); [[/jsxgraph]]

Calculate the total surface area of the frustum. Give your answer as an exact expression in terms of \(\pi\).

[[input:ans1]][[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

node.description: Checks for the correct calculation for surface area of the frustum
Using the vertical height instead of the slant height

truefeedback.text:
Sorry your answer is incorrect.

Your answer suggests that you used the vertical height instead of the slant height when calculating the curved surface area.

Using the vertical height gives

\( A =\pi\left( {@R@}^{2} + {@r@}^{2} + ({@R@}+{@r@})\times{@h@} \right), \)

which evaluates to

\( \boxed{{@mistake1@}\text{ cm}^{2}}. \)

However, the curved surface area uses the slant height, not the vertical height.

First calculate the slant height:

\( s=\sqrt{{@h@}^{2}+({@R@}-{@r@})^{2}} ={@s@}\text{ cm}. \)

Then substitute this value into the formula \( A=\pi\left(R^{2}+r^{2}+(R+r)s\right). \)

Incorrect

Your answer indicates that you used \(R-r\) instead of \(R+r\) in the curved surface area formula.

This gives

\(A=\pi\left({@R@}^{2}+{@r@}^{2}+({@R@}-{@r@})\times{@s@}\right),\)

which evaluates to

\( \boxed{{@mistake2@}\text{ cm}^{2}}. \)

The curved surface area of a frustum is

\(\pi(R+r)s,\)

so the two radii should be added, not subtracted.

The correct expression is

\( A = \pi\left( R^{2}+r^{2}+(R+r)s \right). \)

Incorrect.

Your answer suggests that the slant height has been calculated incorrectly.

It appears you used

\(s=\sqrt{{@h@}^{2}+{@R@}^{2}-{@r@}^{2}}={@l_wrong@}\text{ cm},\)

which leads to

\(A=\pi\left({@R@}^{2}+{@r@}^{2}+({@R@}+{@r@})\times{@l_wrong@}\right),\)

giving

\(\boxed{{@mistake3@}\text{ cm}^{2}}.\)

The horizontal side of the right triangle is the difference of the radii,

\({@R@}-{@r@},\)

so Pythagoras should be applied as

\( s = \sqrt{ {@h@}^{2} + ({@R@}-{@r@})^{2} } = {@s@}\text{ cm}. \)

Using this value in the surface area formula gives the correct answer.
